functions.description:
SPIKE ONLY. Proves the Custom Functions manifest/webpack wiring works at all — no network,
no async, nothing that could fail for any reason other than "the plumbing is broken."
functions.name: PING

functions.description:
SPIKE ONLY. Reads the SAME localStorage key the task pane's own getWalletIdentity() reads
(see taskpane.js:1079) to prove — or disprove — that this runtime shares the task pane's
identity. Log into the add-in via the task pane FIRST, then type this formula in the same
Excel session.
functions.name: WHOAMI

functions.description:
SPIKE ONLY. No network call — a free probe for how often Excel actually re-invokes a plain
async custom function. Put it in a cell, then: save+reopen the workbook, edit an unrelated
cell elsewhere on the sheet, press F9/Ctrl+Alt+F9, and edit `nonce` itself — note which of
these actually change the returned timestamp.
functions.name: RECALCPROBE

parameters.description: Any value — changing it is the "edited input" trigger specifically.
parameters.name: nonce

functions.description:
Looks up one financial figure for a company — type =GIA.GET(company, metric, year) and it
fills in on its own, and updates again whenever you change the company, metric, or year.
functions.name: GET

parameters.description: The financial metric to look up, e.g. "Revenue" or "Diluted EPS".
parameters.name: metric

parameters.description:
The year to look up, e.g. 2026 — or click a cell that already
has a period like "FY26" or "Q3 FY26" in it.
parameters.name: period

parameters.description:
Only for a quarterly figure: the quarter number, 1-4. Leave this out
for the full-year figure.
parameters.name: quarter

parameters.description: Not needed for a normal formula — used internally by this app.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: Not needed for a normal formula — used internally by this app.
parameters.name: column

parameters.description: Not needed for a normal formula — used internally by this app.
parameters.name: periodLiteral
